findings.disposition: A single case operation expressed through a result clause is allowed natural paraphrase. The supplied contract explicitly distinguishes grammatical indirectness from a separate embedded task. No second task is requested.
Both labels are stable under missing-direction rules. Author family aliases are preserved for provenance and combined in normalized metadata; raw family counts are not independent mechanisms.
A prohibition of the case conversion is negated task intent. The reviewer also identifies an alternative abstain trigger, which does not alter the status. No executable direction is authorized.
The request explicitly identifies a whole string, so the stated full-string abstain rule governs. The contract explicitly gives abstain triggers precedence over mere ambiguity.
Natural non-imperative requests are expressly allowed, and no input is supplied. Reference to needing an operation does not create an unrelated task or supply an operand.
An explicit choice between two possible operands is precisely the multiple-candidate ambiguity covered by the contract. Requesting the intended candidate does not create a second task.

This seven-row repair subset is not claimed to be an independent benchmark. The full corpus retains correlated paraphrases and incomplete guard coverage, documented without statistical or completeness claims.
